title: Bacterial Wilt in Solanaceous Vegetables - Nepal

Header: Bacterial Wilt in Solanaceous Vegetables - Nepal

Prevention: Choose a field and neighbouring area without prior history of bacterial wilt disease.
Do not grow solanaceous plants in known infested fields.
Use well drained and leveled fields and maintain good drainage in the field.
Remove any volunteer host plants and solanaceous weeds like
Plant commercially-available, clean, and certified organically-produced tomato seedlings/potato seed/tubers.
Use grafted seedlings of wilt-resistant wild eggplant ( Solanum sisymbriifolium ).
Apply soil solarization for seed bed.
Grow crops in ridge and furrow system.
Avoid root injury during intercultural operations.
Follow crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops, e.g. pea, cowpea, cauliflower, rice, maize, sorghum, wheat, carrots, soybean, sugarcane etc.
Sanitise the equipment that has been used for infected plants before using in healthy plants.
Avoid flood irrigation as this is a waterborne pathogen.
Monitoring: Monitor crop daily for sudden wilting of plants in the field.
Split the stem and check for vascular discoloration (streaking) in basal stem of wilted plants.
Perform test by cutting basal stem of wilted plant for milky strands of bacterial ooze in a clear tube or a glass of water from cut face.
Seek advice on how to do this.
Take action as soon as you have observed a single wilted plant.
Direct Control: Uproot and bury infected plants (at least 50cm deep) outside the field or burn.
Take extreme care not to spread the pathogen.
Drain field as quickly as possible after rains.
Isolate the diseased area by making furrows to reduce the spread of bacteria to non- infested parts of the field.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Drench with copper oxychloride (COC) 50%WP @ 2 g/litre water, enough to wet basal
collar and rhizosphere of plant for 2 times at 7 days interval.
